verdict.rationale: The Zapier Platform CLI docs list webhooks alongside polling triggers as an integration-building capability, and one community user says Zapier made it easy to implement a webhook. Neither item explicitly documents exposing a custom inbound URL that starts a workflow run with the request payload. The Trigger Inbox API's "trigger inboxes and their messages" spec hints at inbound handling but does not describe it. Missing for 10: first-party docs for a catch-hook URL that triggers a Zap, documentation of how the payload maps into the run, auth or URL management details, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can expose a custom webhook URL that receives external HTTP requests and starts a workflow run with the payload

citations.quote: Zapier Platform CLI enables developers to build integrations using Node.js v22, OAuth1/OAuth2 authentication, webhooks, polling triggers, and HTTP middleware.
I am using Zapier because their service was very easy to implement a webhook for what I needed
